title: Ar-Rahim, the Most Compassionate
hook: the Most Compassionate, mercy that reaches each one, closely

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ar-Rahman: mercy overflowing, and a treaty where the name gave way for peace. Your line was mercy covers all. Where did you notice it falling on every field? Day two hundred thirty-six.

After a battle, captives are brought into Medina. Among them is a woman who is frantic, searching every face, every corner. She has lost her baby. Whenever she finds a small child among the captives, she lifts it, presses it to her chest and feeds it, again and again. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is watching with his companions, and Bukhari and Muslim record what he asked them: do you think this woman would ever throw her child into a fire? They said, no, never, not if she could help it. Yesterday was mercy like the rain, falling on everything. Today is mercy like that mother's arms. Today: Ar-Rahim, the Most Compassionate.
screen: `A MOTHER SEARCHING EVERY FACE.` → `ANY CHILD, HELD CLOSE.` → `WOULD SHE THROW IT IN A FIRE?`

segments.voice: The Prophet said: Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child. Ar-Rahim comes from the same root as ar-Rahman, r-h-m, and they almost always travel together: bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim, in every surah but one. So why two names from one root? Scholars have given several answers, and they fit together. The form of ar-Rahman means full and overflowing. The form of ar-Rahim, fa'il, means ongoing, the one who keeps on doing it, again and again. So ar-Rahman is mercy as vast as the sky; ar-Rahim is mercy that arrives, that reaches this particular person, today. Many commentators add a second difference: ar-Rahman is mercy for all creation in this world, and ar-Rahim is a special mercy for the believers, especially in the next. The Qur'an says in al-Ahzab that He is ever merciful to the believers, rahim. Here's a surprise. Unlike ar-Rahman, the word rahim can describe a person. In Surah at-Tawbah the Prophet himself is called ra'uf rahim, kind and merciful to the believers. That makes Ar-Rahim a name you can imitate, and the Prophet said so. In Tirmidhi's collection: the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Have mercy on those on the earth, and the One above will have mercy on you. Mercy close up isn't an idea. It's a mother holding a child close. It's someone showing up.
screen: `MORE MERCIFUL THAN THIS MOTHER.` · `ONE ROOT, TWO NAMES.` · `VAST AS THE SKY; ARRIVING TODAY.` · `A MERCY YOU CAN IMITATE.` · then, large: `MERCY CLOSE UP.`

segments.voice: Sit, and bring one person to mind. Someone who could use a little mercy today. Maybe they're struggling. Maybe they're tired, or alone, or carrying something nobody sees. Picture their face. Now picture one small, specific thing you could do for them: a message, a coffee, not correcting them this once, letting them go first. Keep it tiny and real. Hold that picture for a few breaths. If you pray, you can ask ar-Rahim for them by name. The bell holds the time.
Ar-Rahim. The Most Compassionate: mercy that keeps on arriving, reaching each one closely, and a mercy people are asked to imitate. Today's word.
Your line: mercy close up. Today, do the small, specific thing for the person you pictured, and don't tell anyone you did it. Day two hundred thirty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims say ar-Rahim with ar-Rahman in every bismillah, and many take the hadith of the merciful being shown mercy as a daily rule: kindness to family, neighbors, strangers and animals.

fork.setup: the Prophet points to a mother holding her child and asks: would she throw it in a fire? what does he say next?
options: Allah is more merciful to His servants than she is to her child
fork.reveal: Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman to her child (Bukhari; Muslim).

original.note: Arabic: the Most Compassionate, mercy that keeps on reaching; from r-h-m.

trapdoor: what you thought: ar-Rahim repeats ar-Rahman.
what it means: mercy that keeps arriving and reaches each one closely, a mercy people are asked to imitate.
what a scholar hears: fa'lan (fullness) vs fa'il (ongoing act); many say ar-Rahim is special to believers (33:43); 9:128 uses rahim of the Prophet.

notes: Hadith numbers (Bukhari 5999, Muslim 2754, Tirmidhi 1924) cited from memory; confirm.
The hook's retelling of the captive mother follows the hadith but adds scene detail; the report says she took any child she found among the captives and nursed it; confirm.
The distinction between ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim is presented as several complementary scholarly views; confirm.
